name: MountingPlateDrawing
description:
A three-view drawing of examples/mounting_plate.json, dimensioning the parameters that plate declares. One base view with the other two projected from it, which is how a drafter builds a sheet and which is what makes the stated projection angle mean something: this sheet is first angle, so the TOP view is drawn BELOW the FRONT view. In third angle the same recipe puts it above, and nothing else about the recipe changes. Written against a real shipped part rather than a fixture, because a schema nobody has pointed at a whole recipe is a schema whose gaps have not been found yet -- the argument ARCHITECTURE.md makes for keeping the examples executable.

WHICH DIMENSION GOES ON WHICH VIEW IS THE PART OF THIS FILE THAT WAS MEASURED WRONG FIRST. A view direction here means what INVENTOR means by it, and Inventor is Y-up: `front` shows the XY plane, so on this plate -- sketched on XY and extruded upward in Z, as every recipe here models -- the FRONT view is the PLAN and the TOP view is the 120 x 8 elevation. That reads backwards and it is deliberate; docs/DECISIONS.md has the reasoning. It decides this file: plate_w, plate_d and corner_r are dimensions of the XY outline and belong on FRONT, while thk is the extrude's own distance along Z and can only be shown on TOP. The first version of this recipe had them the other way round, and the 2026-09-08 run reported four of six parameters simply not arriving -- a retrieval can only offer what the view actually shows.

AND edge_margin IS THE ONE THAT STILL CANNOT ARRIVE, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THIS FILE. Asking to dimension it does NOT put 12 mm on the sheet. Dimensions are retrieved from the model, and this model never states 12 anywhere -- the margin is expressed as a hole spacing of `plate_w - 2 * edge_margin`, so what the sheet can carry is 96 mm. The holes are pinned either way and the drawing is correct; the number the recipe named is simply not a number a reader sees. `build_drawing_from_recipe` warns about exactly that, and the rehearsal cannot: the rehearsal resolves edge_margin to 12 because that is what the parameter is worth, and only a sheet that has actually been made can say which dimension came back. That difference between the two directions is the whole reason the round trip reads the sheet rather than trusting the request, and it is why edge_margin stays in this recipe: it is the live demonstration.
notes: REMOVE ALL BURRS AND SHARP EDGES
MATERIAL AND FINISH PER PART RECORD
